headline: Report: Apple launching updated iMac with M6 chip and new colors later this year
summary: Apple is reportedly working on a new iMac, two years after its last major redesign. The upcoming model is expected to feature the M6 chipset and a refreshed color palette.
details: After a two-year hiatus, Apple is gearing up to release an updated version of its iMac desktop computer. This new iteration is expected to incorporate the next-generation M6 chipset, promising enhanced performance and efficiency.

In addition to the internal upgrades, the upcoming iMac is also slated to feature a selection of new color options. This move follows the successful introduction of a vibrant color range with the previous M1-powered iMac, suggesting Apple is keen to maintain its appeal to a broad audience.

The report indicates that the updated iMac will be launched later this year. While specific details regarding the M6 chip's specifications or the exact new colors remain unconfirmed, the refresh signals Apple's continued commitment to its desktop lineup.

topic: legality of training ai models on copyrighted books is complex
headline_marked: [[AI training on books]] legality is complex, courts weigh fair use
headline: AI training on books legality is complex, courts weigh fair use
summary: Authors' works are used to train AI models without consent, sparking legal battles over copyright and fair use. The law is still catching up.
details: AI models like ChatGPT are trained on vast datasets including millions of books, raising questions about copyright infringement. Many authors find their work used without permission to develop tools that could potentially impact their careers.

Legal experts note that current laws are struggling to keep pace with AI advancements. A judge compared an LLM's ingestion of text to a writer's study of literature, suggesting a potential avenue for AI companies to argue fair use.

However, a past case involving Thomson Reuters suing Ross Intelligence for using its content to build a competing AI legal platform set a precedent. The court ruled that Ross's use was not transformative and directly competed with the original content.

While authors may argue that AI chatbots using their works to generate new content are direct competitors, this argument has not yet been definitively settled in court. The legal landscape remains uncertain.
The outcome of ongoing litigation will shape how AI models are trained and how copyright law applies. Both AI companies and creators are closely watching these developments.
